subject: POC prompt set & eval plan — next steps and data collection
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Walters <tom.walters@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: POC prompt set & eval plan — next steps and data collection

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great demo earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC prompt/eval collection so we can kick off the trial next week: 

Summary of ask:
- Acme to share a representative prompt set (JSONL preferred) + a sample of anonymized conversational logs (CSV/JSON) so our SEs can build the eval harness.
- Define success criteria (business KPIs) we should measure during the POC (latency targets, quality thresholds, pass rates per intent).

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
1) Ingest prompt set + logs -> create test splits (train/validation/eval)
2) Run Redwood-hosted inference with recommended model variants and quantization profiles
3) Compute metrics: response accuracy (intent-level), top-N correctness, latency (p50/p95), and qualitative assessment on a 100-sample set
4) Weekly sync to review results and iterate on prompts

Timeline (target):
- Share sample prompts/logs: by end of week (Fri 6/20)
- Redwood processes and initial eval: 3 business days after receipt
- Review call: within 5 business days of initial run
Owners:
- Acme data: Samantha (primary), Tom (technical)
- Redwood: Marissa (sales), Dev Patel (SE lead), Marcus (on-call infra)
Ask for Acme: please send a small sample (100-500 prompts) with expected/desired responses and any labeling you already have. If PII exists, please redact or mark fields to be redacted.
Attachments: I'll attach our POC eval template so you can drop in examples.
Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call to walk through the template.
Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachment: POC_eval_template.xlsx

Cc: Tom Walters <tom.walters@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt set & eval plan — next steps and data collection

Thanks Marissa —

Appreciate the clear plan. We pulled together a small sample and attached: acme_prompts_sample.jsonl (100 prompts) and a redacted snippet of conversation logs acme_conversation_logs_2026-06_anon.csv. Notes on data: 
- We removed PII (names, emails) and replaced with tokens (e.g., [NAME]) where possible.
- Each JSONL line has the fields: id, prompt, expected_response, intent, confidence_label (if available).
- The logs are sessionized; we included a session_id column.

Preliminary success criteria from our side: 
- >= 85% intent-level accuracy on core billing/intake intents across the eval set
- p95 generation latency < 800ms (we run on request-heavy endpoints)

Tom will follow up with a link to the full export (we have ~2k historical prompts). We can host the full export on a shared Drive or provide an S3 presigned URL.

We're also curious about options for on-prem/private ingestion for the full logs due to compliance — Tom, can you coordinate offline with Redwood SEs?

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee | Customer Success Manager
Acme Corp
samantha.lee@acme.com

Attachment: acme_prompts_sample.jsonl, acme_conversation_logs_2026-06_anon.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt set & eval plan — next steps and data collection

Hi Samantha — thanks for sending the samples, this is helpful. A few quick clarifying Qs so we ingest correctly: 

1) JSONL schema: can you confirm the exact keys present in acme_prompts_sample.jsonl? You mentioned id, prompt, expected_response, intent, confidence_label — are there any nested metadata fields we should expect? (we prefer flat keys).
2) Response format: for expected_response, is that a single canonical string, or are there multiple acceptable responses per prompt? If multiple, please include an array or a pipe-delimited list and note expected matching strategy.
3) Long-context prompts: do any prompts include >2048 tokens of history? If so, indicate or tag so we can select compatible model configs.
4) Evaluation labels: what pass/fail criteria do you want for fuzzy matches? (strict exact-match, token-overlap threshold, human-labeled pass/fail). We can support exact, token-F1, and a configurable semantic similarity threshold.
5) For the logs CSV: what columns indicate timestamps/session ordering? We need event_time + session_id to reconstruct conversation context.
6) For compliance: would you prefer uploading the full export to S3 with a limited TTL presigned URL, or would you like Redwood to spin up a Private ingestion endpoint (VPC) for direct transfer? Our Private option is available for regulated data.

Small deliverable from our side: I attached a copy of the POC_eval_template.xlsx with the column mapping we expect. If you can confirm the schema and a sample of multi-acceptable-responses, we'll prepare the initial eval run (goal: within 3 business days of full export).

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: POC_eval_template.xlsx

From: Tom Walters <tom.walters@acme.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC prompt set & eval plan — next steps and data collection

Dev/Marissa —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers and next steps: 
- JSONL schema: flat keys only. Example line: {"id": "12345", "prompt": "How do I reset my password?", "expected_response": "Use the 'Forgot password' link...", "intent": "password_reset", "confidence_label": "high"} 
- Multiple acceptable responses: we have a canonical canonical_response plus an "alt_responses" field in our full export (pipe-delimited in the sample). We can expand to an array if helpful.
- Long context: majority are short (<512 tokens), but there are ~120 sessions with longer histories — we can tag those with long_context=true in metadata.
- Logs: csv has session_id,event_time,sender,message_text columns. event_time is ISO timestamp.
- Compliance: we can provide an S3 presigned URL (see link) or arrange a Private upload. For now we will upload the full export to the shared Drive and send an s3 presigned link for direct ingestion.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-ExampleSharedDrive
S3 sample link (presigned): s3://acme-exports/prompt-exports/2026-06-20-sample.jsonl (will send presigned later)

We'll work on expanding alt_responses to arrays and provide a mapping file. For Private ingestion, our security team will need an architecture note — Samantha, can you coordinate with Redwood SEs on an NDA/SCIF if needed?

Tom
Tom Walters | Principal Engineer, Acme Corp
tom.walters@acme.com

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Below is the agreed plan and owners; please confirm and we'll schedule the review sync.

Agreed evaluation plan & success criteria:
- Data ingest: Acme to provide full export via S3 presigned URL or Drive by EOD Fri 6/26. Redwood to pull and validate schema within 24 hours.
- Metrics: intent-level accuracy >= 85% on core billing/intake intents; p95 latency < 800ms on recommended config; qualitative score >= 4/5 on a 100-sample human review.
- Handling: Redwood will only use the provided data for this POC; logs will be retained for 30 days unless otherwise requested. For regulated data, we can proceed with Private ingestion (Redwood Private) — Marcus will coordinate infra/provisioning.

Timeline & owners:
- 6/26: Acme uploads full export (Samantha/Tom)
- 6/27: Redwood validation and initial run (Dev Patel lead)
- 7/01: Results review call and rubric walkthrough (Marissa to schedule)

Next steps for Acme:
1) Confirm upload method (S3 presigned or Drive) — please include instructions for any vault/NDA sensitivity.
2) If you can, update alt_responses to arrays in full export (Tom offered to do this).
3) Confirm any additional success criteria or metric tweaks.

I'll send a calendar invite for 7/01 for a 45-min review. If that date doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the eval running.
Best,
